Hypothesis: We hypothesize that an advanced dual-mode nanoparticle system, optimized through a combination of passive and active targeting strategies and integrated with state-of-the-art real-time imaging and dosimetry, can synergistically augment BNCT efficacy in boron-avid cancers. Specifically, this system is designed to: (1) maximize selective tumor targeting and boron uptake using enhanced permeability and receptor-mediated endocytosis; (2) utilize an environment-sensitive release mechanism that, informed by real-time imaging feedback, precisely and adaptively co-delivers a PARP inhibitor in synchrony with neutron irradiation; and (3) thereby, promote a scenario where BNCT-induced high-LET radiation creates focal DNA double-strand breaks and the timely PARP inhibition prevents DNA repair, leading to an accumulation of unrepaired DNA damage and enhanced tumor cell death. This hypothesis leverages contemporary imaging and dosimetric technologies to fine-tune treatment timing and dosing, ensuring the highest therapeutic index.
Abstract: We propose an advanced dual-mode nanoparticle system for Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT) that integrates precision tumor targeting, real-time imaging/dosimetry, and an environment-sensitive co-delivery of a PARP inhibitor. The nanoparticle is engineered to maximize selective boron uptake via both passive and active targeting strategies and is equipped with a smart release mechanism that is triggered by specific tumor microenvironment signals. Critically, integrated imaging and dosimetry modules provide real-time feedback on boron distribution and local DNA damage, allowing for adaptive synchronization of neutron irradiation with optimal PARP inhibitor release. This refined design aims to ensure that high-LET radiation induces focal double-strand DNA breaks, while the timely release of PARP inhibitors effectively impairs DNA repair processes. The consequent accumulation of unrepaired DNA damage synergistically enhances tumor cell death, offering a highly controllable, patient-specific treatment modality with improved efficacy and safety over conventional approaches.
CausalChain: Advanced nanoparticle design with integrated imaging/dosimetry -> Enhanced selective boron uptake via dual targeting (passive EPR and active ligand interactions) -> Real-time monitoring of boron distribution and DNA damage kinetics -> Adaptive neutron irradiation triggers high LET-induced DNA double-strand breaks -> Tumor microenvironment triggers precision release of PARP inhibitor -> PARP inhibition impairs repair of radiation-induced DNA damage -> Synergistic accumulation of unrepaired DNA damage enhances tumor cell death
